page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance features 8 virtual CPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. A key hardware characteristic is the inclusion of 1919 GB of local SSD storage, managed via a KVM hypervisor. The network configuration provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the CPU performance of the ecs.i2ne.2xlarge is generally modest. Both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested servers, a trend mirrored by its Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth performance varies, with small-block cached reads performing in the bottom 25%, while large-block uncached read and write operations achieve average tier results. Cryptographic and compression tasks show limitations, with single-threaded gzip compression falling into the bottom 10% and Passmark CPU encryption scoring in the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.i2ne.2xlarge lies in its high local storage capacity versus its lower-tier compute performance. While the 1919 GB local SSD provides substantial space for data-heavy operations, the underlying Intel Xeon 8163 processor exhibits weak performance in compute-intensive workloads, such as medium-sized LLM inference and database operations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance is optimized for scenarios requiring high storage density and moderate memory capacity rather than raw processing power. It is best suited for workloads such as local caching, storage-heavy applications, and moderate database operations where local disk capacity is prioritized over high CPU throughput.
